summary: Clean on the SEC dimension. call.py is a pure compile-time codegen intrinsic with no runtime/untrusted-input surface: the only string input (func_name) is required to be a Python-source literal and must resolve in the trusted signatures dict, and every size/offset feeding an alloca, bitcast, or pointer-pass is derived from compile-time numba types (never caller-supplied or C-returned lengths). The SEC-relevant surfaces named in the notes (extern-ref resolution rather than literal addresses; the presence-only address_of_symbol check) are the documented-correct patterns. No bounds-validation gap, format string, SQL, path loading, C-string copy, or attacker-influenced integer arithmetic exists in this file.
